newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CSR hits out at ACCC on sugar.
newsitem.headline: CSR hits out at ACCC on sugar.

text.p: Building materials, sugar and aluminium group CSR Ltd said on Monday that anti-monopoly watchdog the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) was enforcing competition rules too severely on attempts to rationalise the refined sugar industry.
CSR chairman Alan Coates told the group's annual meeting he was not optimistic the ACCC would approve projects to rationalise the industry, which was heavily over-supplied and suffering a price war.
"We believe they're applying these rules a bit too severely and a bit too according-to-the-book," Coates told the meeting.
"If ever there's an example of what's going on, it's in refined sugar."
Earlier attempts by CSR and other sugar refiners to jointly cut supply and cooperate were rejected by the ACCC, but the industry is again trying to restructure.

CSR said last year it was in talks with other industry players, including Mackay Refined Sugars Pty Ltd, a joint venture between the Mackay Sugar Cooperative and international commodities firm E.D.&F. Man.
"It's a long, hard battle and we're not winning and I don't think we will win," Coates said at Monday's meeting.
